findings.title: Continue-link email builds tokenized resume/erasure URLs from the request origin (X-Forwarded-Host trusted for any *.run.app host)
findings.detail: handle_continue_link derives the emailed base URL via http_origin.canonical_origin(req); canonical_origin prefers x-forwarded-host and is_trusted() accepts ANY host ending .run.app (charset guard only blocks markup smuggling). The endpoint is public: an attacker owning any free .run.app hostname POSTs with a victim's email + the vacancy code, and the victim's genuine Resend email carries their live 288-bit continue/erasure token to the attacker's domain — one click exposes the saved application PII (resume) or deletes it (erasure). The established emailed-link precedent (confirmation email /erase/ link, application_handler.gleam:2121) builds from vacancy.origin_domain via email_client.build_entity_url, never from request headers. All other canonical_origin uses are response-local SSR canonical/OG tags where poisoning only affects the requester — this is the first use that persists a request-derived origin into email sent to a third party.
findings.recommended_fix: Build the emailed base from vacancy.origin_domain via email_client.build_entity_url (the application_handler.gleam:2121 precedent); keep canonical_origin strictly for response-local SSR tags.

findings.title: Stage-2 reminder continue-link only reaches drafts with a pre-minted token; auto-saved drafts (token NULL) get the plain 'Start your application' URL
findings.detail: Frozen AC (spec-form-save-resume-f3.md:100): 'Given a stage-2 reminder to an enquirer with a draft ... its CTA is the tokenized continue-link'. Tokens are minted only by claim_continue_link_send (the 'Email me a link' button), so debounced-auto-save drafts — the exact abandonment cohort the D+6 'continue where you left off' reminder exists to recover — have NULL tokens, are filtered out (continue_token IS NOT NULL), and get the pre-F3 generic CTA; their drafts are unreachable from the email. The E2 seam (briefing requirement 5) silently no-ops for the majority cohort.
findings.recommended_fix: Mint tokens for tokenless live drafts at reminder-prefetch time (UPDATE ... SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, <random>) WHERE submitted_at IS NULL before the SELECT), so every live draft maps to a continue-link CTA.

findings.title: form_draft.test.js claims E2E coverage by a bug-hunt save-and-resume scenario that does not exist; fetch/beacon/button choreography untested at any level
findings.detail: The header asserts the browser choreography 'is covered E2E by the canonical bug-hunt scenario for save-and-resume'; grep of .claude/skills/bug-hunt/scenarios/ finds no save/resume/draft/continue scenario. The spec's own Tests task (spec line 93) scopes beacon/copy-swap coverage to this suite. The save-trigger listener, saveNow flow, pagehide beacon, continue-button flow and prep-note swap have zero coverage — deleting the rt:form-step-changed listener kills all draft saving with every test green.
findings.recommended_fix: Author the cited save-and-resume bug-hunt scenario (save on step change -> draft row -> continue-link -> resume pre-filled -> submit stripped), and/or factor saveNow/beacon into injectable factories (apply_analytics.js createCapture precedent) for node tests; correct the stale comment.

findings.title: Self-service draft erasure is silently undone by any still-open form tab (hard DELETE, no tombstone for re-save)
findings.detail: Applicant confirms Art. 17 erasure (e.g. on phone); a laptop tab with the form still open then step-saves or pagehide-beacons, and the upsert re-INSERTs the full PII payload — erasure left no row for the ON CONFLICT WHERE to reject (the submit path got exactly this tombstone guard: submitted_at IS NULL; the erasure path did not). The confirmed deletion is reversed without anyone knowing; resurrected PII persists until vacancy close.
findings.recommended_fix: Make erasure a tombstone (fields='{}', continue_token=NULL, erased_at stamp the upsert's WHERE rejects, retention sweeps later) instead of a hard DELETE — mirror the strip-on-submit pattern already in this diff.

findings.title: Retention sweep deletes drafts on vacancy ARCHIVE, contradicting the emailed 'expires when the vacancy closes' promise and destroying drafts on a restorable state
findings.detail: Archive is distinct from close (listed separately in the SQL) and per AGENTS.md archiving is 'restorable anytime'. The daily sweep permanently deletes drafts the moment a vacancy is archived; if the landlord restores it, saved answers and emailed continue links are dead — while the continue email (spec line 84: 'expires when the vacancy closes') promises otherwise.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete drafts only on closed/closes_at, or sweep archived-vacancy drafts only after an archive-age threshold; align the email copy with the actual rule.

findings.title: Unauthenticated draft-save has no per-vacancy or per-IP bound — fabricated-email rows accumulate until vacancy close
findings.detail: The abuse model considers PII visibility, not volume: the upsert keys on (vacancy, email), so invented emails yield unlimited rows up to 64 KB each; nothing rate-limits the write (Cloudflare's single ruleset rule covers /erase//dsar/; the worker buckets cover authwrite/payment-verify/consent only) and retention sweeps only at vacancy close.
findings.recommended_fix: Per-vacancy draft cap (reject new keys past N) and/or a per-IP bucket for /apply/:code/draft in the Cloudflare worker.

findings.title: Public continue-link endpoint sends real Resend email with no per-IP limit — draft + continue-link combine into an email fan-out vector
findings.detail: An attacker creates drafts for any (vacancy, victim-email) via the unauthenticated save, then triggers official branded email to each victim. The 10-min cooldown is per-draft only; nothing bounds fan-out across distinct recipients (no server limiter; no edge rule covers /apply/:code/continue-link). Resend spend + sender-reputation risk; combined with B1 the emails carry poisoned origins.
findings.recommended_fix: Per-IP bucket for /apply/:code/continue-link (worker rateLimitBucket pattern), keeping the per-draft cooldown as second layer.

findings.title: Strip-on-submit wiring in finalise_application untested — deleting the call fails no test
findings.detail: The strip SQL and late-save race are integration-pinned, but every test seeds the stripped state via direct SQL; no full handle_post_form test asserts finalise actually calls strip_draft_on_submit. A regression removing the call passes green; pre-submit PII then lingers until vacancy close.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend an existing successful handle_post_form integration test: seed a draft for the submitter email, submit, assert fields='{}', continue_token NULL, submitted_at set.

findings.title: list_resumable_draft_tokens SQL + stage-2 recipient->continue-URL mapping have zero coverage
findings.detail: The F3xE2 seam (briefing requirement 5) has its SQL filter (submitted_at IS NULL, token IS NOT NULL), email-lowercase mapping, and prefetch-failure degradation untested (grep server/test: zero references). Only the email template branches are unit-tested; the data path feeding them is not.
findings.recommended_fix: Integration test seeding live/submitted/tokenless drafts asserting only live tokenised rows return (awaiting_integration_test.gleam is the natural home); optionally extract the continue-url selection as a pure function with unit tests.

findings.title: Resume GET on a closed vacancy (frozen I/O matrix: 'existing closed page') unpinned
findings.detail: Drafts survive vacancy close until the daily sweep, so a continue-link click in that window hits the is_accepting_applications=False branch. The branch exists (view_closed_vacancy_page) but no test would fail if it regressed to rendering a restored form on a closed vacancy; the save endpoint's closed branch IS tested, the resume one is not.
findings.recommended_fix: Integration test: seed closed vacancy + draft with token, GET resume, assert the closed-vacancy page renders (no form-resume marker).

findings.title: Test named 'never keeps a file shaped key' never sends a file-shaped key; the pinned filter would keep one
findings.detail: The name asserts a key-shape rejection the body never tests; filter_fields keeps ANY non-underscore, non-gdpr_consent key <=64 chars — a hand-crafted file-input-named key would be kept (by design, as a <=4000-char scalar). False assurance on the spec requirement-4 'no documents in drafts' claim; only the inline comment states the real contract.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename the test to what it pins (scalar pass-through + 4000-char cap), or feed a real file-slot-named key and assert the intended rejection.

findings.title: form.js form-resume anti-clobber guard (deliberate backdate protection) has no test pin
findings.detail: The server half (backdated _form_loaded_at render) is pinned by resume_page_backdates_the_timing_field_test, but the client guard that keeps form.js from clobbering it is untested (form.js has no test file). Reverting the guard re-opens the <2s anti-bot black-hole for honest resumed submits with all tests green.
findings.recommended_fix: Node test stubbing document.body with data-apply-page=form-resume before requiring form.js, asserting the pre-set _form_loaded_at survives.

findings.title: Debounced save uses POST where the frozen I/O matrix specifies PUT (beacon excepted)
findings.detail: Frozen matrix + spec task line say the debounced save is a PUT (POST only for sendBeacon, which requires it); saveNow POSTs. Router maps both verbs to the same handler (router.gleam:790-793), so purely documentary drift — but spec text, the line-226 comment and code now disagree, and the spec change log doesn't record it.
findings.recommended_fix: Switch saveNow to PUT (beacon stays POST), or amend the frozen matrix's Save row to POST and note the refinement.

findings.title: Spec frontmatter declares status 'done' while its Tests task checkbox remains unchecked
findings.detail: Every other task is [x]; the Tests line is [ ] while the document asserts done and the suites it names did ship. Either the checkbox is stale or the status premature.
findings.recommended_fix: Tick the Tests checkbox (the named files exist and pass) or adjust it to reflect genuinely outstanding work.

findings.title: Unused import gleam/option in the new integration test file (compiler warning on every build)
findings.detail: Six lenses independently confirmed: import present, zero references in the file. PR-introduced warning noise in a previously warning-quiet suite.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete line 10.

findings.title: Local list_length helper re-implements gleam/list.length (six call sites)
findings.detail: Hand-rolled, non-tail-recursive duplicate of the stdlib; the same PR's draft_handler_test.gleam imports gleam/list and calls list.length. Inconsistent with the codebase pattern.
findings.recommended_fix: import gleam/list, replace the six list_length call sites, delete the helper.

findings.title: application_draft.updated_at maintained manually; mark_draft_resumed_by_token and clear_last_link_sent omit it
findings.detail: Repo convention maintains updated_at via the generic update_updated_at_column() trigger (vacancy, ai_analysis, reference_call migrations). The draft table has no trigger; two of five writers leave updated_at stale.
findings.recommended_fix: Add CREATE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column() (reference_call pattern); drop the manual sets.

findings.title: SSR form assembly (8 sections + honeypot/timing + script block) triplicated across the three form-page renderers
findings.detail: Same section list + script block in view_application_page (form_view.gleam:80), view_form_with_errors (:339), view_resume_page (:416). This PR proves the cost: adding view_draft_saver_script() required the identical edit at three sites.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract shared view_form_sections(values, errors, loaded_at_ms) + view_form_scripts() helpers; renderers differ only in marker, banner/prep block, timing stamp.

findings.title: handle_save_draft and handle_continue_link repeat the decode/validate/lookup/filter preamble plus a verbatim resumed-stamp block
findings.detail: Lines 146-157 and 216-233 repeat require_json/decode/email-validate/lookup_accepting_vacancy/filter_fields; the mark_draft_resumed block appears verbatim twice. Only the failure posture differs (500 vs 200-abort).
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a shared staging helper returning Result(#(DraftPayload, vacancy, uuid, filtered), Response) and a stamp_resumed helper; keep only the divergent upsert-failure handling.

findings.title: validEmail comment + test name claim near-miss emails still save, but currentPayload gates the save on them
findings.detail: Comment: 'a near-miss email still saves (server rejects), it just won't gate the save locally' — but currentPayload returns null when validEmail fails, so a near-miss (e.g. tenant@example) blocks the save locally. Behavior matches the spec matrix; the prose (and test name 'rejects the near-misses that must not gate a save') contradicts it.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword comment + test name: locally-implausible emails block the save.

findings.title: Cross-file DOM event-name contract (rt:draft-saved / rt:form-step-changed) test-pinned on neither side
findings.detail: form_draft.test.js never asserts EVENT_DRAFT_SAVED or EVENT_STEP_CHANGED values. If the emitter's string drifts from the listener's (form_stepper.js / apply_analytics.js), the save hook and analytics relay break silently with no failing test.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin draft.EVENT_DRAFT_SAVED === 'rt:draft-saved' and draft.EVENT_STEP_CHANGED === 'rt:form-step-changed' in form_draft.test.js.

findings.title: No fetch capability check despite 'capability is real' copy-swap promise (sendBeacon/CustomEvent guarded, fetch not)
findings.detail: On a fetch-less browser the prep note is swapped to the save-and-continue promise and the button injected, but saveNow and the click handler throw synchronously (no promise chain, .catch never runs). Contradicts the file's progressive-enhancement header. Marginal (fetch is near-universal) but inconsistent with the file's own guards.
findings.recommended_fix: Add if (typeof root.fetch !== 'function') return; to initBrowser before the copy swap and button injection.

findings.title: Clean pagehide beacon from the resume page stamps resumed_at with zero re-engagement
findings.detail: resumeToken rides every payload including the pagehide beacon; no dirty/baseline tracking on the resume render, so open-and-close (or a JS-firing mail scanner) stamps resumed_at although the applicant never engaged — partially defeating the anti-prefetch re-engagement rule the SQL comment describes.
findings.recommended_fix: Seed the client baseline with the restored payload on the resume render (or set a dirty flag on first input/step event); include resume_token only after real engagement.

findings.title: Submit-time strip matches only the final form email — drafts keyed under an earlier/edited email keep their PII
findings.detail: Drafts key per (vacancy, email); a typo then correction creates a second row. The strip at finalise targets only the submitted email, so the earlier row's field payload survives until vacancy close with no continue-link owner aware of it.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept as vacancy-close-bounded residual (document it), or strip all rows for the vacancy matching any email used this session / add a TTL for stale unsubmitted drafts.

findings.title: get_draft_by_continue_token selects resumed_at and vacancy_id that no handler reads
findings.detail: Resume consumes id/fields/submitted_at; erasure-confirm consumes email; nothing reads vacancy_id or resumed_at. Dead surface in a generated row type.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the two columns from the SELECT/row type, or use vacancy_id to cross-check the route code instead of the JOIN alone.

findings.title: continue-link 'sent' flag is a submission-status oracle, contradicting the 'never reveals' header comment
findings.detail: Anyone knowing the applicant's email + vacancy code can poll with an empty fields map (skips upsert, claims against the existing draft): sent:true flips to permanent sent:false exactly when the victim submits (submitted_at set -> claim matches no row). Low impact; the header claims the response never reveals whether a draft exists.
findings.recommended_fix: Answer sent:true even when the claim returns zero rows (client copy already reads cooldown and sent identically); keep ok:false only for genuine failures.

findings.title: draft_handler docs overstate the response contract: 'Always 200' vs claim-failure 500; 'Errors are JSON' vs text/plain 500 arms
findings.detail: Two internal doc/code mismatches: (1) continue-link doc says always 200 on well-formed payloads, but a claim DB failure returns wisp.internal_server_error() while an upsert failure returns 200 ok:false; (2) lookup_accepting_vacancy doc says errors are JSON, but its DB/uuid arms return text/plain 500.
findings.recommended_fix: Pick one failure posture for claim/upsert (or fix the comment); reword the JSON-errors doc or return JSON 500s.

findings.title: 'Byte-identical to pre-F3 stage 2' comment is false: the shared checklist paragraph changed in this PR
findings.detail: Both stage-2 branches call requirements_checklist_html(), whose closing paragraph this PR rewrote ('You don't have to finish in one visit...'), so the no-continue_url email is NOT byte-identical to pre-F3. The comment misleads anyone verifying the funnel split.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: 'identical except the CTA/saved-line' (the checklist change applies to both variants), or drop the claim.

findings.title: New unit test uses deprecated list.range (compiler warning)
findings.detail: list.range(1, 200) in a new file; project convention is gleam/int.range.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace with int.range(1, 200) + import gleam/int.

findings.title: apply_analytics.js rt:draft-saved relay + form-resume funnel suppression unpinned at wiring level
findings.detail: Only the outcomeEvent mapping and event-name constants are pinned; the relay listener and the form-resume funnel early-return have no wiring-level test. Metrics-only; matches this file's pre-existing norm.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional hardening: extract the marker->wiring decision into an exported pure function (createAbandonFlow precedent) and pin form-resume suppressing section events.

findings.title: PostHog token-scrub asserted only via the pristine apply page; resume-page tests pin no snippet property
findings.detail: Factually true, but low-risk: all four renderers (incl. view_resume_page, form_pages.gleam:437) call the same shared view_posthog_snippet helper the test pins, so the scrub cannot regress on the resume page without touching pinned shared code. Demoted from blind's warning on verification.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: one assertion that view_resume_page output contains sanitize_properties, pinning the wiring not the logic.

findings.title: Body-size rejection arms tested with POST only; PUT rejection unpinned
findings.detail: The at-limit allow test exercises both verbs; over-limit, missing-content-length and transfer-encoding rejections use Post only. A Put arm that skipped the 64 KB cap would pass every test.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror the over-limit (and ideally missing-CL) assertions with http.Put on the draft route.

findings.title: The advertised 10-minute cooldown value is never pinned — only an immediate re-claim is asserted
findings.detail: Cooldown tests stamp last_link_sent_at = now() (inside the window); no test backdates past 10 minutes asserting the claim succeeds. A 1-hour or 1-day interval in the SQL passes these tests identically.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a claim test with last_link_sent_at = now() - interval '11 minutes' asserting the claim returns a row.

findings.title: draft_field unwraps query failure to '', so empty-string assertions pass when the row is missing
findings.detail: Assertions like draft_field(db, other_id, 'resumed_at') |> should.equal('') are satisfied by an absent row as well as by an empty column, masking the state they claim to pin (contrast draft_count's fail-closed unwrap(-1)).
findings.recommended_fix: Return a sentinel (e.g. '<query-failed>') or assert row existence separately.

findings.title: With-draft reminder test never asserts the plain CTA is gone — both buttons could render
findings.detail: The without-draft test pins 'Continue where you left off' absent, but the with-draft test lacks the symmetric negative on 'Start your application'. A template rendering two competing CTAs at the F3xE2 seam passes all tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Add html |> string.contains('Start your application') |> should.be_false to the with-draft test.

findings.title: Comment says 'Since F3 shipped' inside the PR that ships F3
findings.detail: Past-tense framing in the F3 diff itself; will mislead future archaeology about when the one-visit copy died.
findings.recommended_fix: Present tense: 'F3 replaces the one-visit rule with the save-and-continue promise.'

findings.title: Resume-page backdate test fails spuriously if >1s elapses between its two clock reads
findings.detail: view_resume_page stamps now-10_000ms; `v < before` (before = current_unix_ms() - 9000) holds only while the render's internal clock read runs <1000ms after the test's. A >1s scheduler stall fails correct code.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert a relative window: capture after = form_view.current_unix_ms() post-render; check before - 10_000 <= v <= after - 10_000.

findings.title: resumed_at stamp-once (COALESCE) and submitted-guard boundaries unpinned
findings.detail: Only the first stamp is pinned. A regression dropping COALESCE (second save moves resumed_at, corrupting the resume funnel) or the submitted_at IS NULL guard passes all tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend first_post_resume_save_stamps_resumed_at_test: save again with the token, assert unchanged; optionally assert a stripped draft never stamps.

findings.title: handle_continue_link send branches (Resend success/failure shaping, upsert-failure abort ordering) verified only manually
findings.detail: Claim/mint/cooldown/clear SQL is fully covered and one handler-level cooldown test exists, but the response-shaping branches around the Resend call and the abort-on-upsert-failure ordering have no test (Resend itself is not integration-testable; the branches around it are, via a forced DB error).
findings.recommended_fix: Cover the upsert-abort branch by forcing a DB error (killed connection) in an integration test; the E2E scenario in W2 covers the happy-path send.

rejected_findings.title: strip_draft_on_submit email is not trimmed, but the draft-save path trims — whitespace mismatch leaves draft PII unstripped
rejected_findings.reason: False premise: the submit side passes get_form_value(values, "email"), which trims (application_handler.gleam:2276 'Ok(value) -> string.trim(value)'). The strip key is byte-identical to the upsert key (handler trims, both SQL statements lower()). Verified by direct read.
